purpose: Separate AI exposure, implementation, worker voice, control, and realized worker outcomes in the broad trend atlas.

sources.exposure_or_implementation: AI task adoption, customer-support and knowledge-worker experiments, and education/task performance comparisons
sources.worker_outcome: issues resolved, email time, task adoption, and experimental performance; pay, discretion, bargaining, and household security remain open
sources.boundary: separate study units and designs; adoption or measured productivity does not establish worker control or distribution

sources.exposure_or_implementation: algorithmic-management tools, employer monitoring, reported AI use, executive expectations, and union representation
sources.worker_voice_or_control: governance measures and formal representation are reported, but worker decision rights are not linked to adoption
sources.worker_outcome: reported productivity/employment expectations and formal representation rates; no same-workplace worker outcome
sources.boundary: cross-source comparison with incompatible units, periods, and denominators; no causal workplace chain

sources.exposure_or_implementation: work-related AI use and algorithmic-management practices
sources.worker_voice_or_control: collective bargaining, works-council review, data access, public action, and legal challenge
sources.worker_outcome: reported rule changes including consent/pay, monitoring limits, human oversight, and restored discretion; unresolved cases remain
sources.boundary: comparative EU and qualitative case evidence, not a US population estimate or realized average effect

sources.exposure_or_implementation: controlled Copilot and Places rollout, tolerance phase, approval, training, permissions, DLP, and dashboards
sources.worker_voice_or_control: works-council concerns reached product engineering; Places country targeting and default opt-out are company-reported
sources.worker_outcome: not independently observed; no worker-level productivity, workload, privacy, pay, stress, or enforcement outcome
sources.boundary: company-reported implementation account; consultation and product change are not proof of worker acceptance or durable control

sources.exposure_or_implementation: AEDT use is covered by a bias-audit, public-summary, and employee/candidate-notice requirement
sources.worker_voice_or_control: workers and candidates have a complaint route; discrimination claims are referred to the NYC Commission on Human Rights
sources.worker_outcome: no named employer implementation, worker decision change, appeal, compensation, or workload/pay/health outcome located
sources.boundary: official rule and access-route pages; no public case-level outcome or defined complaint denominator, so no compliance or welfare estimate

sources.exposure_or_implementation: FLSA guidance addresses AI and automated workplace systems including surveillance, targeting, and analytics within existing labor standards
sources.worker_voice_or_control: anti-retaliation and labor-standard obligations provide an enforcement vocabulary; worker decision rights are not directly observed
sources.worker_outcome: no named implementation, worker exposure, changed decision, enforcement disposition, correction, or compensation located
sources.boundary: federal interpretive guidance and public source surface; not an employer-use rate, worker outcome, or compliance estimate

program_result: AI/work evidence is strongest at exposure, adoption, organizational implementation, and consultation/design stages. It is weaker at same-workplace worker control, enforcement, distributional outcomes, household security, and bargaining change.
next_test: Follow one named workplace system from implementation through worker notice, negotiated rule, actual exposure, override/appeal, workload/pace, pay, schedule control, health, bargaining, and household outcome, with a comparable non-exposed or differently governed workplace.
storage_boundary: Uses committed local records and one committed local implementation memo; no raw-data acquisition or new estimate.
